name: Boat24
notes: Europe-wide brokerage and private listings. It refuses anything that is not a browser — even its home page answers 403 to a plain request — so this source is rendered in WebKit. Boat24 files by builder rather than free text, so the name goes straight into the path: /en/sailingboats/grinde/. Verified: that page lists a Grinde in Germany at EUR 25,000.

name: Tradera
notes: Sweden's largest marketplace (eBay-owned), auction + fixed price. SSR HTML, no rendering needed. Verified 2026-09-13: 35 cards on a search page, title/url/price/image all present. No location on cards. No pagination links found — pages pinned to 1. Prices print as '175 kr,' — the SEK defaultCurrency tells the price parser which krona this is.

name: Bazos.sk
notes: Slovakia's big free classifieds site. Primitive stable HTML, no bot wall. Verified 2026-09-13: 'gibson' returned 20 of 112 results with title/url/price/image/summary/place all parsing. Space-grouped prices ('1 699 €'). Pagination exists ('Dalšia') but its href wasn't captured during scouting — pages pinned to 1 until verified.

name: Bazos.cz
notes: Czech Republic's Bazos — same software and markup as bazos-sk, so the same selectors hold. Verified 2026-09-13: 'gibson' returned 20 cards, all fields parsing. Prices in CZK ('31 000 Kč'). Pages pinned to 1 as with bazos-sk.

name: Scanboat
notes: European boat market (Denmark-based, boats across the EU), SSR HTML — no rendering needed. Verified 2026-09-13: 'grinde' returned 12 cards with title/url/price parsing on all; some cards lack image or catchphrase. Country is embedded in body text ('| Country : Germany') with no clean selector, so no place field. No pagination found — pages pinned to 1.

name: Reverb
notes: Global music-gear marketplace. Hard TLS-fingerprint wall: plain HTTP gets 403 even with browser headers, so this source is rendered in WebKit. Verified 2026-09-13 through the app's own BrowserFetcher: 'gibson' returned 60 cards with title/url/price/image on every one. Prices are USD. No location on cards. Some item links carry a long tracking parameter — harmless. No pagination found — pages pinned to 1.

name: Subito
notes: Italy's biggest classifieds site. Plain HTTP returns a client-rendered shell with no listings, so this source is rendered in WebKit. Verified 2026-09-13 through the app's own BrowserFetcher: 'gibson' rendered 42 cards with title/url/price/image/place on every one. Prices are dot-grouped euros ('1.200 €'). Hashed CSS-module classes (index-module_*) are build-stable for this codebase. No pagination found — pages pinned to 1.

name: Willhaben
notes: Austria's largest marketplace. Plain HTTP gets a JS shell; rendered in WebKit, the page embeds __NEXT_DATA__ with the full search result — read as nextdata. Verified 2026-09-13: 'gibson' returned 30 adverts, title/url/place/image on every one. The url is willhaben's /iad/object?adId= resolver, which 308-redirects to the public listing page. No price field: prices live in an attributes array whose order varies per advert, and no path reliably selects it — listings ship without a price until the walker can filter by attribute name. contextLink index 5 and attribute index 0 (LOCATION) were stable across all 30 sampled adverts.
